# TRILOGY AT REDMOND RIDGE RESIDENTIAL DESIGN GUIDELINES Exterior lighting refers to any lighting to be mounted on a residence, within the Unit landscape or elsewhere on the Unit. Lighting plans shall include manufacturer specifications, i.e., type of fixture, number, color, voltage, and bulb wattage/lumen requirements (see RDG 4.6.3 and 4.6.4 below) in addition to placement and installation details. Landscape lighting and lighting on the buildings should be used sparingly and tastefully with special consideration given to the impact on neighbors, wasteful energy consumption, and unnecessary light pollution. Up-lighting is restricted under King County Regulations. All up-lighting is limited to 25 watts or 200 lumens. Acceptable uses of lighting are to facilitate safe access for the residents and use of the yard, including the creation of landscape interest. Lighting should be understated and not distracting. Light sources (bulbs) should be shielded as much as possible. The following restrictions shall apply: 4.6.1 All light fixtures above or below grade shall be installed and shielded so as not to produce glare onto neighboring properties, streets, or forested areas. This also applies to decorative lighting, such as rope lights, string lights, and LED strip lights. 4.6.2 All fixtures must use incandescent, halogen, LED, or compact fluorescent lamps (CFL). Colored lamps, including lamps sold as "bug lights," or "party lights" are not allowed. Mercury vapor lights are also prohibited. 4.6.3 Low wattage lights and warm white bulbs (2700K) are recommended. Bulbs must conform to the following for externally mounted fixtures on houses such as front entry, garage, patio and/ or deck: 25W/200L, 40W/450L, or 60W/800L. Bulbs must not exceed 60W/800L. 4.6.4 For landscape, patio, spa, and deck installations, bulbs must be low voltage (12V), not to exceed 200 lumens. Owners are requested to use light fixtures where light is directed downward rather than outward. The Reviewer will consider post mounted lights on a case-by-case basis. 4.6.5 For walkway/ path installations, bulbs must be low voltage (12V), not to exceed 200 lumens. Owners are requested to use light fixtures where light is directed downward rather than outward. 4.6.6 Deck, stairway, or fence mounted light fixtures shall be consistent with the architecture of the Unit. The fixtures shall be designed to conceal the source of light with the light directed downward from a position on the deck, stairway, or fence no higher than 4 feet. Landscape lighting added to Association Maintained Areas of the Unit cannot interfere with landscape maintenance and shall be the responsibility of the Unit owner. 4.6.7 Rear and side yard lighting shall be used in moderation and shall not cause excessive glare or light spillage onto adjacent Units. 4.6.8 Security lighting on a Unit shall be limited to lighting that is triggered by motion on the Unit (but not by motion on neighboring properties) and reasonably illuminate only the area of the Unit immediately surrounding the residence. Such lighting shall not be directed at any neighboring properties. Motion detectors shall be programmed to shut off # TRILOGY AT REDMOND RIDGE RESIDENTIAL DESIGN GUIDELINES the light(s) within 5 minutes of when a motion is detected, and the light has been illuminated. 4.6.9 All exterior lighting, except for carriage and pathway lighting, shall be shut off between the hours of midnight and 5:00 a.m. Carriage lighting refers to wall mounted, or recessed lighting installed by the Developer in the entry and garage areas of the unit. Motion detectors as described above are permitted during these timeframes. No other options will be considered. 4.6.10 Soffit lighting is approved for holiday use only with no distracting patterns, no over-glare and no spillage between homes, and cannot be used as security lighting. Lighting plans shall include manufacturer specifications (i.e., type of fixture, number, color, voltage and bulb wattage/lumens per RDG Article 4.6.3 and 4.6.4) in addition to placement and installation details. Installation shall consist of a small, aluminum channel behind and flush with the bottom of the fascia board, and the channel color should match the color of the fascia board. Holes in the channel for lights shall be spaced evenly at a minimum of 9 inches apart and low voltage (30 lumens) lights installed through the holes. Holiday lights cannot be displayed more than thirty days before and after the holiday. ## 4.7 Yard Ornaments [COMPLIANCE ONLY] Yard ornaments include but are not limited to sculptures, fountains, statues, benches, animal replicas, pottery and any attachments or adornments to the exterior of the house. Yard ornaments do not require approval before installation or display. Consideration should be given to the general aesthetics of the community and the visual and auditory impact on neighbors. Ornamentation should conform to the following: 4.7.1 Ornamentation that is visible from streets should be used sparingly and tastefully so that its appearance is understated and not distracting. 4.7.2 Be of a design that is appropriate to a well-maintained community. 4.7.3 In relation to the home site, be reasonable in number, proportion, color, material, and appearance, and cause no obstruction to Association Maintained Areas. 4.7.4 Not be of a theme that is offensive or controversial. ### 4.8 Fire Hydrant Clearance Per King County Code (KCC 17-08-030): 4.8.1 There shall be thirty-six (36) inches of clear area around the hydrant to allow for operation of a hydrant wrench on the outlets and on the control valve. 4.8.2 Hydrants shall not be obstructed by any structure or vegetation. nor shall the visibility of the hydrant be impaired for a distance of fifty (50) feet in the direction of vehicular approach to the fire hydrant. # TRILOGY AT REDMOND RIDGE RESIDENTIAL DESIGN GUIDELINES ## Article 5 Fences, Gates, and Walls ### 5.1 Fences, Gates, and Walls A consultation with Association Staff is encouraged. Owners should be aware that King County may have specific code requirements for fences and walls. The Design Review Committee's approval does not assure compliance with King County Code. Replacement of fences and gates on a like for like basis requires DRC APPROVAL. ### 5.2 Fence Styles #### 5.2.1 Wood Fence Styles. Wood fences and gates shall consist of vertical boards, horizontal rails, and post caps. Horizontal boards are not permitted. Tall, consecutive sections of lattice shall not be used as a material or style for wood fencing. See Exhibits K, L and M for the specific approved wood fence styles. See RDG 5.5 for limitations on use of lattice on wood fences. See RDG 6.12 for guidelines on Landscape Screenings, Lattices, Trellises, Arbors, and Pergolas. #### 5.2.2 Composite Fence Styles Composite fence can be a combination of a polymer and non-polymer additives. The fence should be a K style. Other styles may be considered on a case-by-case basis. #### 5.2.3 Metal Fence Styles. Metal fences and gates shall be 2-rail or 3-rail open metal view fencing with a maximum 4-inch picket spacing. A 3-rail open metal view fence with closer pickets in the bottom half of the fence is also allowed. No other alternatives will be considered. See Exhibit N for the specific approved metal fence styles. See RDG 5.7 for additional guidelines for fencing abutting the golf course. #### 5.2.4 Invisible underground fences are not permitted. #### 5.2.5 Horizontal style fences are not permitted ### 5.3 Fence Materials Only wood, composite, and open metal view fencing materials may be used for enclosing yards and creating privacy. No other materials, including vinyl, are permitted. #### 5.3.1 Wood Fence Materials. Posts, stringers, or K-Banding shall be cedar or pressure-treated material. #### 5.3.2 Composite Fence Materials The homeowner shall comply with manufacturer's recommended construction guidelines, including posts. Approved Manufacturers include:
(i) TREX
(ii) FRAME IT ALL
(iii) NEOLINE
(iv) Others on a case-by-case basis
## TRILOGY AT REDMOND RIDGE RESIDENTIAL DESIGN GUIDELINES ### 5.3.3 Metal Fence Materials. Open metal view fences shall be constructed of fabricated tubular metal with black powder coat finish. See RDG 5.7 for additional guidelines for fencing abutting the golf course ### 5.4 Fence Colors #### 5.4.1 Wood Fence Colors. (i) All above grade portions of newly installed or replacement wood fences shall be stained. If only fence sections are replaced, they shall match the other sections for uniformity. (ii) The fence color may be used in a solid or semi-transparent stain color only. No transparent stains are allowed. (iii) Fence colors are limited to the following: a) Behr: Cedar: (SC-146) AND Drift Gray (SC-137) b) Benjamin Moore: Natural Cedar tone (ES-45) and Alexandria Beige (HC-77) c) Sherwin Williams: Cedar (SW-3034) and Kings Canyon (SW-3026) d) Other brown and grey tones will be considered on a case-by-case basis, provided a sample of the color and picture of the house is provided with the application. (iv) Re-staining Existing Wood Fences. When re-staining becomes necessary or required by the Association for maintenance, wood fences shall be re-stained using a solid or semi-transparent stain color approved by the Design Review Committee per RDG 5.4.1.ii, and 5.4.1.iii. (v) The specific wood treatment shall be identified on the application. (vi) Wood fences shall be stained on both sides (vii) Any lattice, arbor, or gate associated with a wooden fence shall match the fence color. #### 5.4.2 Composite Fence Colors (i) The composite fence colors shall be limited to those available through the following Manufacturers: a) TREX: Winchester Grey and Saddle b) FRAME IT ALL: River Birch and Teak c) NEOLINE: Honey Oak and Desert Sage (ii) The specific color of composite fences shall be identified on the application. (iii) Any lattice, arbor or gates associated with a composite fence shall match the fence material and color. (iv) Fence posts shall match the fence color. #### 5.4.3 Metal Fence Color All open metal view fences shall have a flat black powder coat finish. ### 5.5 Fence Height Limitations #### 5.5.1 Wood and Composite Fence Height Limitations (i) The maximum height of fences constructed along or on Unit boundary lines or return fences from the side yard boundary to the house, is 72 inches (6 feet), and the minimum height of any fence constructed on a Unit is 40 inches. ## TRILOGY AT REDMOND RIDGE RESIDENTIAL DESIGN GUIDELINES (ii) The lattice component on any fence shall not exceed 18 inches and the total height of the fence and lattice shall not exceed 90 inches (71/2 feet). Only standard 2-inch diagonal or square lattice shall be approved. See Exhibit O for approved lattice styles. (iii) Arbors may be added to the top of fences, but the total height of fence, lattice and arbor combinations shall not exceed 96 inches (8 feet). ## 5.5.2 Metal Fence Height Limitations (i) The height of metal fences constructed along or on a Unit boundary, including boundaries shared with the golf course, shall be between 4 feet and 6 feet. Variations from this height may be considered by the Reviewer for specific circumstances. ### 5.6 Placement of Fences #### 5.6.1 Fences to Separate Units Side and rear yard boundary fences may be placed: either on the boundary line (property line) that separates neighboring Units, or that separates a Unit and adjacent Common Area; or fences may be placed along the boundary line but totally within the boundary of a Unit. (i) Boundary Line Fences Side and rear yard boundary fences placed on boundary lines that separate neighboring Units or fences that are attached to fences on other Units, require the approval of the neighboring Unit Owner in the DRC application packet stipulating the following: a) That the neighboring Unit Owner approves the placement and height of the fence and the materials to be used. b) That the neighboring Unit Owner understands and agrees that the fence constitutes a "party structure" as described in Declaration 13.1 and that the Owner will be responsible for maintenance and repair of a portion of the fence; and c) That the neighboring Unit Owner understands and agrees that the new fence will attach to an existing fence and may require joint maintenance responsibility among the Owners. (ii) Non-Boundary Line Fences If a neighboring Unit Owner does not approve a fence being placed on the boundary line, then the Owner desiring the fence may construct it alongside the boundary lines of his/her Unit. This is a Non-Boundary Line Fence. As such, all elements must be entirely within his or her property. The DRC application packet from any Owner electing to build a Non- Boundary Line fence shall stipulate the following: a) That the fence is not a "party structure" as described in Declaration 13.1, and b) That the Owner will be responsible for maintenance and repair of both sides of the fence. #### 5.6.2 Fences within Front Yards Applications for front yard fences will be evaluated in terms of their compatibility with the overall appearance of the streetscape. The following parameters apply to fences constructed within front yards: #### TRILOGY AT REDMOND RIDGE RESIDENTIAL DESIGN GUIDELINES (i) Placement of front yard fences should consider curved streetscapes and other aesthetic details and must not interfere with a driver's ability to see objects in the roadway. Refer to RDG 5.8.4 below. (ii) Front yard fences and fences constructed between side yard fences and the house should be placed no less than 5 feet behind the nearest front corner of the house. Windows and utilities may require other setbacks. Other considerations will be case-by-case. (iii) In cases of uniquely shaped Units, uncommon placement of the home and/ or driveway on the Unit, or unusual orientation of the home to adjacent homes, the Reviewer will determine the front, side, and rear yards of the Unit. (iv) Any areas maintained by the Association should remain accessible. ##### 5.7 Golf Course Fences 5.7.1 Any fence installed on or along a boundary line between a Unit and the golf course shall be an open metal view fence. 5.7.2 Side yard fences on Units that abut the golf course shall be open metal view fences from at least the point where the Unit abuts the golf course to a point 10 feet from the golf course boundary. A greater distance may be required by the Reviewer to accommodate view corridors. ##### 5.8 General Fence Considerations 5.8.1 Boundary Line Locations. Verifying the location of Unit boundary lines prior to construction of fences is the sole responsibility of the Owner(s) constructing the fences. 5.8.2 Easements. Unless otherwise prohibited on a recorded plat or other recorded document, an Owner may construct fences within utility easements. However, if removal or alteration of the fence is required by the utility company to exercise its rights under the easement, any such removal or alteration shall be at the sole expense of the Owner. Plot plans should be examined to see if there are driver or pedestrian sight line restrictions. 5.8.3 Fencing Installed Near Sidewalks, Streets and/ or Driveways. The Reviewer may require that fencing installed near sidewalks and/ or driveways be located such that plantings may be required to soften the appearance of the fence. The reviewer may also require that new fencing along streets in the public view be built with horizontal deviations to prevent long, uninterrupted lengths of fencing and provide areas for plantings. A set-back of 3 to 5 feet may be required for visibility, aesthetics, or other safety reasons. 5.8.4 Visibility. The Reviewer will consider the impact of a proposed fence to driver visibility. Adverse impact may require modification to the application before it can be approved or could result in denial of the application. 5.8.5 Maintenance. See the Trilogy Board Rules and Regulations, Article 4.2.3, for maintenance standards for fences. 5.8.6 Disputes. If a dispute between Owners arises with respect to the maintenance, repair or replacement of a party structure, the dispute shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of Declaration Article 14. ###### 5.9 Gates 5.9.1 Gates for Wood and Composite Fences. Gates on wood and composite fences shall coordinate with the adjacent fence types and be substantially the same height as the adjoining fence. # TRILOGY AT REDMOND RIDGE RESIDENTIAL DESIGN GUIDELINES 5.9.2 Wood or composite gates may have lattice or arbor on top, but the total height may not exceed 7.5 feet (90 inches) and with an arbor no more than 8 feet (96 inches). See Exhibits K, L and M. 5.9.3 Gates for Metal Fences. Gates on metal view fences shall match the material and color of the metal fence and be substantially the same height as the adjoining fence. See Exhibit N. 5.9.4 Gates for Courtyard Entries. Material for front courtyard entry gates shall be limited to Open View Metal fencing (Exhibit N). Other metal options will be reviewed on an individual basis. Size and style will be considered in relation to the style of the home. 5.9.5 Fences between Units and Common Areas shall not be altered by an Owner to install a gate. ## 5.10 Landscape Privacy Screening (Aesthetic, Shading, Privacy) 5.10.1 A screen is defined as a fixed, flat, protective partition shielding an area from view, from heat or drafts, from light, or providing privacy and shall not be on a property line. A screen may be used as an architectural feature. Homeowners may erect a wide variety of screening devices for aesthetic privacy or shading purposes. Owners must get the approval of the Association Staff or Design Review Committee, prior to submitting a proposal and application. 5.10.2 Screens may be constructed with wood, composite, or metal materials. The colors for screens shall follow the guidelines outlined in Article 5.4. 10.3 Screens may not exceed 16 feet in length or 8 feet in height. The DRC shall consider exceptions to these dimensions based on the lot, the size of the house, or surrounding properties. 5.10.4 Wood or composite material utilized for screening may be used horizontally if the area is under 16 feet in length. Anything beyond 16 feet must use vertical planks. ### 5.11 Utility Screening (Air Conditioners, Generators, Heat Pumps, and Garbage Cans) 5.11.1 Garbage cans shall be screened by fencing or landscaping to not be visible from neighbors, street, or golf course. 5.11.2 Screens may not be placed forward of the front corner of the house for typical lot configuration. Exceptions may be considered in unusual situations where the placement of the house on a given lot may pose a unique challenge. Total concealment from the street view is mandatory from all angles. 5.11.3 3 Small wooden screening devices intended to conceal trash cans, AC units, generators, or heat pumps can be stained with a stain that complies with Article 5.4, or a solid or semi- transparent color that matches the body color of the house. Metal and composite materials will be considered. 5.11.4 Materials and designs for screening devices shall be compatible with the home. 5.11.5 Shrubbery shall also be considered acceptable concealment but must provide concealment from street view from all angles. 5.11.6 Screening around public utilities is prohibited.

Article 5 Fences, Gates, and Walls
5.1 Fences, Gates, and Walls

A consultation with Association Staff is encouraged. Owners should be aware that King County may have specific code requirements for fences and walls. The Design Review Committee's approval does not assure compliance with King County Code. Replacement of fences and gates on a like for like basis requires DRC APPROVAL.
5.2 Fence Styles
5.2.1 Wood Fence Styles.

Wood fences and gates shall consist of vertical boards, horizontal rails, and post caps. Horizontal boards are not permitted. Tall, consecutive sections of lattice shall not be used as a material or style for wood fencing. See Exhibits K, L and M for the specific approved wood fence styles. See RDG 5.5 for limitations on use of lattice on wood fences. See RDG 6.12 for guidelines on Landscape Screenings, Lattices, Trellises, Arbors, and Pergolas.
5.2.2 Composite Fence Styles
Composite fence can be a combination of a polymer and non-polymer additives. The fence should be a K style. Other styles may be considered on a case-by-case basis.
5.2.3 Metal Fence Styles.

Metal fences and gates shall be 2-rail or 3-rail open metal view fencing with a maximum 4-inch picket spacing. A 3-rail open metal view fence with closer pickets in the bottom half of the fence is also allowed. No other alternatives will be considered. See Exhibit N for the specific approved metal fence styles. See RDG 5.7 for additional guidelines for fencing abutting the golf course.
5.2.4 Invisible underground fences are not permitted.
5.2.5 Horizontal style fences are not permitted
5.3 Fence Materials
Only wood, composite, and open metal view fencing materials may be used for enclosing yards and creating privacy. No other materials, including vinyl, are permitted.
5.3.1 Wood Fence Materials.
